tagline: Guanacaste's most popular first-timer beach town pairs gentle beginner surf breaks with lively nightlife, an easy hour's drive from Liberia International Airport.
overview: Tamarindo was a quiet fishing village until surfers discovered its beaches in the 1970s and the 1994 surf film Endless Summer II put it on the map. Today it is the busiest beach town on Costa Rica's dry Pacific north coast, but the long sandy bay and relaxed 'pura vida' pace remain.

Playa Tamarindo's soft, forgiving waves make it one of the world's best places to learn to surf, while neighbouring beaches like Playa Langosta and Playa Avellanas offer bigger breaks. Between the town and Langosta, the Tamarindo estuary winds through mangroves where boat tours spot crocodiles, howler monkeys and scarlet macaws.

After dark the town comes alive with beach bars, sunset catamaran cruises and restaurants serving everything from fresh ceviche to wood-fired pizza. Day trips reach the Rincón de la Vieja volcano for hot springs and mud baths, and the leatherback turtles of Las Baulas National Marine Park nest just across the estuary.

funFacts.title: A SURF MOVIE MADE IT FAMOUS
funFacts.text: Endless Summer II (1994) filmed at nearby Witch's Rock, turning Tamarindo into a global surf destination.

funFacts.title: GIANT SEA TURTLES
funFacts.text: Las Baulas park next door hosts nesting leatherback turtles, which can weigh over 500 kilograms, from October to March.

funFacts.title: AN EASY ARRIVAL
funFacts.text: Liberia International Airport is only about an hour away, making Tamarindo one of Costa Rica's easiest beach towns to reach.

funFacts.title: CROCODILES IN TOWN
funFacts.text: The Tamarindo estuary is home to American crocodiles that can grow past 4 metres.

funFacts.title: A DRY PARADISE
funFacts.text: Guanacaste's dry season can see almost no rain from December to April — rare for the tropics.

funFacts.title: HOWLERS AS ALARM CLOCKS

funFacts.title: A FAMOUS REEF BREAK
